provenance.name: DREAM4 In Silico 10-Gene Gold Standard Challenge Network
provenance.organism: Synthetic / In Silico (Subgraphs from E. coli & S. cerevisiae)
provenance.technology: Stochastic Differential Equations (SDEs) generated via GeneNetWeaver with non-linear thermodynamic Hill kinetics
provenance.data_type: Steady-state expression ratios under single-gene knockouts relative to wild-type baseline
provenance.perturbation_type: Targeted gene knockouts / knockdowns (10 single-gene perturbations)
citations: Marbach, D., Schaffter, T., Mattiussi, C., & Floreano, D. (2009). Generating realistic in silico gene networks for benchmarking reverse-engineering methods. Journal of Computational Biology, 16(2), 229-239. DOI: 10.1089/cmb.2008.09TT

Prill, R. J., Marbach, D., Saez-Rodriguez, J., et al. (2010). Towards a rigorous assessment of systems biology models: the DREAM3 and DREAM4 challenges. PLoS ONE, 5(2), e9202. DOI: 10.1371/journal.pone.0009202
provenance.overview: The DREAM4 In Silico Network Challenge represents the community standard for reverse engineering evaluation. Network 1 (Size 10) features non-linear cooperative transcription with negative feedback loops and cascades, providing an unambiguous ground truth with signed causal edges (+1 activation, -1 repression).

provenance.wrangling_procedure:
1. GeneNetWeaver numerical integration of stochastic differential equations with Langevin noise.
2. Measurement noise added following micro-array error models (additive + multiplicative normal noise).
3. Expression matrix X formatted as steady-state response relative to wild-type.
4. Perturbation matrix U set to diagonal single-gene interventions.

how_raw_data_is_used.wrangled_direct: The 10x10 knockout response matrix is used directly by inference algorithms. Tests whether methods can resolve transitive indirect effects (G1 -> G2 -> G3 vs G1 -> G3) and correctly assign feedback loop signs.
how_raw_data_is_used.biophysical_fit: The ground truth topology and knockdown levels calibrate Hill saturation constants K_a, K_i and cooperativity exponents n=2, enabling ODE integration of dynamic perturbation time courses.
